transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’ve been waking up feeling really sad... heavy, I guess. Like there’s this hollow feeling in me. I’m a dancer, and it’s like the studio lights are on, but there’s no music there anymore. That’s what made me think I should come in.
Have you found that you don't enjoy dancing or other things you used to like as much lately?
I’m not sure. I mean, dancing still matters to me, but lately it’s been harder to feel the same spark. I don’t know if I’d say I don’t enjoy it at all… it just feels more muted.
Have you noticed that most days, you feel down or sad most of the day, not just for a short while?
Yes. Most days I wake up with that heavy, hollow sadness, and it tends to stay with me for a lot of the day. It’s not just a quick feeling that passes.
Do you feel this heavy sadness most of the day, nearly every day, or does it come and go more noticeably?
It’s more like most of the day. I wake up with it, that heavy hollow feeling, and it kind of stays with me. Like I said, it’s like the studio lights are on but there’s no music in me.
Have you experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in dancing or other activities you used to enjoy, nearly every day?
I’m not sure I’d say nearly every day. I have noticed it feels harder to really enjoy dancing the way I used to, but I can’t tell if it’s that constant or that clear-cut.
Would you say that you experience this loss of enjoyment in dancing and other activities you used to like on most days, nearly every day, rather than just occasionally?
I’m not totally sure. It does happen, like dancing doesn’t feel as satisfying sometimes, but I don’t know if I can say it’s most days or nearly every day. It’s hard for me to pin down.
Would you say that on most days, nearly every day, you experience a loss of interest or pleasure in dancing and other activities you used to enjoy?
I honestly can’t say it’s nearly every day. I do have times where dancing feels kind of flat, like I’m just going through the motions, but I haven’t really tracked it enough to say it’s most days.
Would you say that on most days, nearly every day, you experience a loss of interest or pleasure in dancing and other activities you used to enjoy?
I still don’t think I can say “nearly every day.” I’ve noticed it comes up sometimes, where dancing or other things don’t feel as enjoyable, but I’m not sure it’s that frequent.
Would you say that on most days, nearly every day, you experience a loss of interest or pleasure in dancing and other activities you used to enjoy?
I don’t think I can say that, no. It happens sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it being most days or nearly every day.
Would you say that on most days, nearly every day, you feel a lack of energy or feel fatigued, even after resting?

Yes, I do feel that. Even small things can wipe me out, like answering one email to a dancer or just showering with this ankle brace on. I’ll lie down after, but it doesn’t really feel like I recharge much.
Have you noticed that you have trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions, nearly every day?
I’m not really sure. I have moments where I feel a little foggy or it takes me longer to decide something, but I haven’t noticed it happening nearly every day.
Would you say that on most days, nearly every day, you have trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions?
I don’t think I’d say it’s most days. I have times where I’m a bit scattered or slow making a decision, but it’s not something I’ve clearly noticed nearly every day.
Would you say that on most days, nearly every day, you have trouble thinking clearly, concentrating, or making decisions?
Like I said, not really nearly every day. I do get foggy sometimes, but I wouldn’t say it’s a constant or most-days problem for me.
Would you say that on most days, nearly every day, you experience a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even outside of dancing?
I’m not sure I’d say nearly every day. I still enjoy some things, and I haven’t really noticed a consistent loss of interest like that.
Would you say that on most days, nearly every day, you experience a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even outside of dancing?
I don’t think so. I mean, I have off days where I don’t feel like doing much, but I haven’t noticed that kind of loss of interest happening nearly every day.
Would you say that on most days, you experience a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even outside of dancing?
No, I don’t think it’s most days. I still get enjoyment from things. Sometimes I’m just not in the mood, but it doesn’t feel like a steady loss of interest.
Would you say that on most days, you experience a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even outside of dancing?

I don’t really think so. I’ve said this a few times, but it’s not like a most-days thing for me. I still enjoy things when I’m actually doing them. Sometimes I’m tired or not up for much, but I wouldn’t call it a loss of pleasure.
Would you say that on most days, you experience a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even outside of dancing?
I don’t think so. I know you’ve asked a couple times, but no—it’s not something I’ve noticed on most days. I still enjoy things, just not every single day feels the same.
Would you say that your heavy, hollow sadness is present most of the day, nearly every day?

Yes… most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow sadness. It’s like I’m there, but there’s no spark in me. I don’t know if it’s every minute of the day, but it hangs around a lot of the day, nearly every day.
Would you say that on most days, nearly every day, you experience a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even outside of dancing?

I’m still not sure I’d put it that way. I have days where I don’t feel like starting anything, but when I do something I used to like, I can still get some enjoyment from it. So no, I haven’t noticed a loss of interest or pleasure nearly every day.
